title: Create: Preformance
description: A modpack made to run Create Mod on computers that couldn't normaly run it!
body:
# Create Performance
**Experience the ingenuity of Create—without the lag.**

**Create Performance** is a carefully curated modpack designed for players who want to dive deep into complex automation and mechanical engineering while maintaining smooth, high-frame-rate gameplay.

Whether you are building massive **industrial factories**, complex train networks, or intricate farms, this pack provides the perfect balance of creative freedom and technical optimization. We’ve hand-selected a suite of essential **performance-enhancing mods** to ensure your game stays responsive, even when your creations grow to massive proportions.

What’s Included:
**Optimized Mechanics**: We’ve built this pack around the latest version of Create, paired with lightweight addons that expand your engineering possibilities without the bloat.

**Performance First**: Using the NeoForge architecture, we have integrated industry-leading optimization mods like **Sodium and Lithium**. This pack is engineered to run consistently well on lower-end hardware and laptops.

**Quality of Life**: Spend more time building and less time managing inventory. We’ve included a selection of refined tools—such as **advanced storage systems**, better recipe viewing, and intuitive mapping—that respect the vanilla feel while drastically improving your day-to-day experience.

A "**Lag-Free**" Guarantee: By prioritizing performance-focused utilities, we have minimized the common stuttering and TPS drops often associated with automation-heavy modpacks.

Built For:
This pack is perfect for players who love the Create mod but have struggled with performance issues in the past. If you want a stable, reliable environment to build your dream factory, Create Performance is for you.

Ready to start engineering? This pack is optimized for 4GB of allocated RAM to ensure the best stability on modest systems. Simply install and jump straight into your world.
